title: Per-tenant embedding endpoint (embedding_base_url) + config-time dimension probe with legible remediation
background: The embedding endpoint is server-wide: config/runtime.exs:382-385 sets %{base_url: OPENAI_BASE_URL || "https://api.openai.com/v1", model: ...}, read at knowledge/embedding_client.ex:194 (@default_base_url at :41, provider_config/0 at :295). Per-tenant configuration today (llm/tenant_llm_settings.ex:41-54) covers api_key, extraction_model, classification_model, merge_model, embedding_api_key, embedding_model - key and model, but NOT endpoint. Importantly the embedding KEY is already per-tenant and MANDATORY (embedding_client.ex:58-60,75-77; the global operator key was deliberately removed in runtime.exs:375-381), so the per-tenant credential plumbing and its MCP surface (set_llm_config) already exist. Adding the endpoint is one field plus one read - not a subsystem.

story.as_a: an agent configuring a tenant that must not send content to third-party providers
story.i_want_to: set the tenant's embedding endpoint to a local or self-chosen OpenAI-compatible server through the same MCP tool I already use for the key, and be told immediately if the endpoint is unusable
story.so_that: embeddings are computed where the tenant chooses, and a misconfiguration fails at config time with a fix I can act on - not hours later as an opaque write error

rationale: This is the smallest change that makes the hosted service usable for a privacy-constrained tenant, and it is the prerequisite for the egress guard in US-41.4 (there is nothing to point at until an endpoint is configurable). The probe exists because loopctl has NO UI: a human would notice a broken endpoint in a settings screen, an agent will not unless the tool tells it.

acceptance_criteria.description: tenant_llm_settings gains embedding_base_url (nullable; NULL means fall back to the server-wide default, preserving today's behavior exactly). embedding_client.ex resolves the tenant value first, the runtime default second.

The field is writable through the EXISTING set_llm_config MCP tool and its matching JSON API endpoint - no new tool, no UI. The tool description states plainly that the endpoint must be OpenAI-compatible (POST /embeddings) and that changing it may require a re-embed (US-41.1 AC-41.1.6).

Config-time probe: setting embedding_base_url (or embedding_model) issues ONE test embedding against the supplied endpoint before persisting. On success the returned dimension is recorded as the tenant's dimension. On failure NOTHING is persisted and the call returns a legible, agent-readable error.

Probe failures are distinguishable and each carries a meta.remediation payload in the same ACTION REQUIRED shape knowledge_search already returns for a missing embedding key: unreachable endpoint, auth rejected, non-OpenAI-compatible response shape, and dimension-not-supported-by-this-instance are four DIFFERENT messages, each naming the concrete next step.
The probe never leaks secrets: the endpoint URL is echoed in errors and posture reports, the API key never is. A test asserts no key material appears in any error body, log line, or audit entry.

The probe is bounded and cannot be used as an SSRF primitive or a DoS lever: it reuses the existing URL guard used by ingestion (workers/content_ingestion_worker.ex:620-632, UrlGuard.pinned_request_opts/1 + redirect: false), has a short timeout, and is rate-limited per tenant.

Default-off and non-breaking: a tenant that never sets embedding_base_url behaves exactly as today, including the mandatory-BYO-key behavior. No existing tenant is re-probed or re-embedded by this story.

test_cases.name: tenant endpoint overrides the server default
preconditions: tenant with embedding_base_url set to a stub local server
expected_results: the request goes to the tenant endpoint
the server-wide default is not contacted

test_cases.name: probe records the dimension returned by the endpoint
unreachable endpoint fails closed with remediation
expected_results: error names the endpoint and the failure class

test_cases.name: each probe failure class is distinguishable
preconditions: four stub endpoints: refuses, 401s, returns non-OpenAI JSON, returns an unsupported dimension
expected_results: four distinct error codes and four distinct remediation texts - never one generic failure

test_cases.name: no key material leaks
steps: inspect error body, logs, audit entries

test_cases.name: probe cannot reach internal addresses when the guard forbids it
preconditions: URL guard configured to reject the target range
steps: attempt to set an endpoint pointing at a forbidden address
expected_results: rejected by the guard before any request

technical_notes: Reuse Loopctl.Vault.Binary for nothing new here - the endpoint is not a secret and MUST be readable by egress_posture (US-41.4). Only keys stay encrypted.

The SSRF consideration cuts both ways: a local_only tenant NEEDS to reach private-range addresses (that is the point), while a hosted non-local tenant should not be able to probe the operator's internal network. Resolve this by making the allowlist policy (US-41.4) govern which ranges are reachable, and have the probe consult the same policy - do not write a second, divergent URL policy here.
Record the probe result (endpoint, dimension, timestamp, outcome) in the audit log - US-41.7 builds the custody claim on top of exactly this record.
Ollama's OpenAI-compatible surface and HuggingFace TEI are the two reference targets; test against stubs shaped like both rather than assuming one vendor's response envelope.
